full_judgment:
9. Plaintiff claims a derivative title from Subhan. According to him Subhan held the suit land in rayati right which was inherited by his heirs, two sons and wife, and they, by a patta, Ext. 4 dated 28-7-54, settled the land with him. Plaintiff in 1955 purchased the superior rayati right of his lessors, and thereby succeeded to the sixteen annas title of Subhan in the suit land. No doubt plaintiff.has produced the Patta Ext. 4, and the Kabla received from the heirs of Subhan one in 1954, and the other in 1955. The question is not the validity of the patta, but whether the lessors of the plaintiff had any transferable right. That again depends upon the fact whether they inherited any such transferable right from their predecessor, Subhan. Is there any evidence to show that Subhan held any tenancy right as claimed by the plaintiff ? The plaintiff except making his own bare assertion, and reliance on R.S. Khatian, Ext. 10, has adduced no evidence, oral or documentary. Plaintiff being a transferee from the heirs of Subhan, has not and cannot claim direct knowledge of the creation of tenancy in favour of Subhan. He could, however, lead evidence to prove the creation of tenancy. That he has not done. His case of title rests on the alleged presumption of correctness of settlement records. 

 10. The High Court has taken a view that although, an entry in the record of right would indicate the possessory right of the person whose name appears therein, but this also lends support to the claim of title made by the plaintiff. It seems to us, that this view of the High Court does not state the correct view of law on the presumption arising from the record of right. Both the learned counsel have on this point, cited a number of decisions. Apart from the cited decisions, there are a large number of authorities on this point, Some of them may be mentioned. Rani Harshamukhi Vs. Kshitindra, 47 C.W.N. 662, Anup Mahto Vs. Mita Dusadh 38 C.W.N. 365 (P.C.), Sri Nath Rai Vs. Pratap Udai Nath Sahi Deo, 28 C.W.N. 145 (P.C.), Pankajini Debi Vs. Suair Dutta 60 C.W.N. 793, Munnalal Vs. Mst. Kashibai 51 C.W.N. 175, Narendra Vs ( Rajendra 45 C.W.N. 654 ; Rai Kiran Chandra Roy Bahadur Vs. Srinath Chakrabarti 31 C.W.N. 135, Kumar Rai Vs. Baraboni Coal A.I.R. 1935 Calcutta 368, Jemarat Ali Vs. Rahman Sardar 17 D.L.R. Dacca 589, Pramatha Nath Vs. Kamir Mondal 17 D.L.R. (S.C.) 392. 

 11. Not all the cited authorities are. directly on the question before us, nor do we feel the necessity of referring to all of them in detail. From the cited decisions, we find that the preponderance of the judicial opinion is that the presumption of correctness arsing from the record of right under s. 103B of the Bengal Tenancy Act raises a presumption of possession in favour of person whose name is recorded therein at the time of its final publication. No forward or backward presumption arises from correctness of record of right. For drawing backward presumption there must be some evidence. Forward presumption however is not available from the s. 103B of Bengal Tenancy Act, but a presumption of continuity may be drawn under s. 114 (d) of the Evidence Act. This forward presumption becomes weaker with the passage of time, and its probative value diminishes progressively with the lapse of time. 

 13. We may now turn to the facts of the case. R.S. Khatian of the plot, Ext. 10, shows a tenancy was recorded in the name of Subhan under, Moifula Khatun. The record of right was published some time in 1927. Initial presumption of correctness of recording of possession of 1927 in favour of Subhan is there. Barring Khatian, the plaintiff has led no evidence on the creation of tide of Subhan. Plaintiff leading no evidence, either oral or documentary, cannot use the Khatian as evidence of title in favour of Subhan. The High Court was wrong in presuming title in favour of Subhan barely relying on Khatian. Bereft of this Khatian, there is no evidence of creation tenancy in favour of Subhan. The plaintiff has failed to prove that the heirs of Subhan acquired any transferable right to confer upon plaintiff by patta Ext. 4 Plaintiff has therefore valid to make out a valid title in his favour on the basis of Patta,
